Subject: Orchestration lanechart & stakeholder fallbacks — MSA/DPA/orderform sequencing

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the demo today. As discussed, we sketched an orchestration lanechart to make the procurement/legal sequencing explicit and to capture fallback paths if the DPA redlines take longer than expected. I attached the lanechart (medsage_orch_lanechart_v1.xlsx) and dropped a short MAP CSV with milestones in the Drive link below.

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm who in MedSage will own the PO / procurement signoff (name + email) and the approximate internal procurement cycle (standard, expedited, or custom)?
- Any org-level constraints on data residency or auditors we should anticipate for DPA review?
- Is DocuSign ok for your legal team, or do you require a different e-sign process?

Our proposed sequencing (draft):
1) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) agreed — target Oct 30
2) Order form signoff (pricing & SOW) — target Nov 5
3) DPA redline / legal signoff — target Nov 12 (we propose parallel review; if DPA extends >2 weeks we can enable limited Dedicated capacity under an interim privacy attestation)
4) Production onboarding & acceptance gates — target Nov 19

Key owners (internal): Laura (legal sequencing), Karthik (onboarding & acceptance), Grace (ops SLA runbooks).

If the proposed dates look reasonable to you, we'll convert the lanechart into a single MAP spreadsheet that both teams can co-edit and surface a DocuSign packet for the order form while legal runs the DPA review in parallel.

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-example-lanechart
Attachment: medsage_orch_lanechart_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —

Rafael —

Appreciate the clear outline. Procurement here — our usual cadence is two weeks for PO review for standard vendors; we can expedite to 5–7 business days if legal confirms there are no material DPA redlines. Our procurement lead is Priya Shah (procurement@medsage.com).

A few clarifications from our side:
- MedSage requires a named DPA reviewer (we'll route to our privacy counsel) and a SOC2 attestation if model-hosted data will include PHI.
- DocuSign is fine; we typically request the order form and PO executed first, then MSA/DPA in parallel.

I attached our internal PO guidelines for reference. Happy to sync on a quick call if helpful.

Subject: Re: Orchestration lanechart & stakeholder fallbacks — MSA/DPA/orderform sequencing

Team —

Reviewed Samir's note and the lanechart. A couple of legal takeaways and a proposed tweak to sequencing:

1) DPA redline window: expect up to 2 weeks for initial comments if MedSage privacy counsel is responsive; 3+ weeks possible if they request bespoke security controls.
2) Order form first: signing the order form (pricing + PO) before full DPA execution is OK but we need an explicit interim data handling attestation in the order form that we can enforce operationally. That attestation should list the environment (dedicated vs hosted), retention windows, and access controls.
3) Fallback: If DPA not final by Nov 12, we should have a pre-authorized path to spin up Dedicated capacity on a reserved pool for MedSage for a 30-day interim while legal completes the DPA. That requires a budget approval flow (Sales -> Finance) and an ops runbook (Grace).

I'll draft the attestation paragraph and drop into the MAP CSV. Rafael — can you confirm if MedSage will accept an attestation clause in the order form (short, operational) while legal finishes DPA? Karthik — once Rafael confirms, please prepare acceptance criteria for the onboarding runbook so ops can provision Dedicated with a checklist.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Samir / Priya (cc'd),

Thanks — that cadence helps. Priya, looping you so procurement timeline and PO expectations are explicit. We've moved the MAP into a collaborative CSV (MAP_v1.csv) and added a short attestation clause Laura suggested. The key decision points we're trying to lock:

- Order form signed by Nov 5 (pricing + PO).
- DPA in parallel; if not signed by Nov 12, Redwood can provision Dedicated capacity under the attestation for up to 30 days while legal completes the DPA.
- Acceptance testing gates owned by MedSage product + Redwood onboarding (Karthik) — acceptance criteria doc will be ready by Nov 10.

Operational asks for MedSage:
- Confirm PO owner (Priya).
- Confirm procurement can target Nov 5 for order form signature assuming standard PO cycle or expedited review.
- Confirm DocuSign is the execution method so we can prepare the packet.

If you give the green light, we'll prepare the DocuSign packet for the order form and the attestation paragraph, and Laura will start the DPA redline loop.

Thanks —
Rafael
